opinions.rationale:
Under an inverted prior, the literature still treats pre-analysis bias bounds for general-population comparator sampling as missing. Heide-Jørgensen et al. (Clin Epidemiol 2018;10:1325-1337; doi:10.2147/CLEP.S164456) remains the central evidence: it demonstrates that sampling without replacement in random order can inflate comparator outcome rates via conditioning on the future, that chronological sampling without replacement fails by exhaustion (nearly one-fifth unmatched at 5:1 in a 347,882 heart-failure cohort, with a younger residual reference arm), and that the three schemes nearly coincide at 1:1 but separate at 5:1 when comparators are at high risk. Its own Discussion states the decisive limitation: the study “did not present means of quantifying the size of these differences in general.” That is documentation of the phenomenon, not a bound recoverable from sampling ratio, pool-to-index size within matching strata, and comparator baseline hazard before sampling is run.

Searches for a later resolving method returned none. Queries covered: (1) the paper’s own limitation language and its citations; (2) “sampling with/without replacement” + “general population comparison cohort” + chronological/random order + bias/bound/quantify, restricted to 2019–2026; (3) AJE, Epidemiology, IJE, EJE, JCE, PDS, Clin Epidemiol, Stat Med, SMMR, Biometrics, Biostatistics, BMC Med Res Methodol, Observational Studies, BMJ/JAMA/AIM, plus arXiv stat.ME/AP and medRxiv; (4) MatchIt, WeightIt, TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp, ltmle, cobalt, and related packages for a pre-analysis bias bound for registry comparator sampling (they implement with/without replacement for propensity matching, a different design); (5) TARGET 2025, Arnold et al. Front Drug Saf Regul 2024, STaRT-RWE/HARPER, ENCePP, FDA/EMA external-control guidance. What appears after 2018 is mostly applied uptake: Danish and other registry studies cite Heide-Jørgensen and default to sampling with replacement (or 1:1). That is a design convention, not a bound. Iwagami (Ann Clin Epidemiol 2022) discusses with/without-replacement tradeoffs for matching but supplies no pre-run bias formula for the three schemes. Austin-style PSM order and with/without-replacement results address treated–untreated matching within a study population, not index-date assignment of general-population comparators under pool depletion. TARGET requires reporting the comparator and its emulation, not the sampling scheme that produced the comparison arm, so the published literature remains largely uninformative for calibration.

A method paper that only proposes or recommends with replacement without evaluating a general bound would still leave the problem open. A sensitivity analysis after sampling would price consequences of a choice already executed, not bound bias from quantities known before cohort construction. No retrieved work derives the comparator-hazard bias as a function of the three pre-sampling quantities named in the agenda, or provides a validated simulation protocol that yields bounds rather than one-dataset case reports. Status therefore remains open; the statement is proportionate to the evidence.
